importance_ranking.reason: Aircraft hangars are engineered-to-order structures; buyers cannot evaluate any listing without knowing span width, eave height, hangar type, and door configuration — these specs define whether the structure can physically accommodate their aircraft. Without matching specs, no buyer engages regardless of image or price.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant consumer-recognisable brand exists in Indian aircraft hangar supply; buyers evaluate sellers by engineering capability, IS 800 compliance track record, DGCA-related project experience, and erection credentials — not brand name recall.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional and defence buyers conduct formal vendor qualification; seller credentials (PEB fabrication capability, past airport/defence projects, IS code compliance, erection experience) are a primary shortlisting gate equal in weight to specifications.

High visual variation across sub-types — PEB clear-span vs T-hangar vs fabric/tensioned structure vs space frame are visually distinct structural forms; buyers use images to confirm structural type and scale before reading specs. A listing showing a generic industrial shed instead of a clear-span hangar is immediately disqualifying.

Every aircraft hangar is custom-engineered to site and aircraft requirements; no fixed list price exists and final value is always project-quoted. Indicative per-sq-ft rates serve as a budget entry point for Indian buyers but are not comparable across listings without spec equivalence.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Turnkey/EPC contracts are quoted as lump-sum per project; fabric/portable hangars may be quoted per piece. Per sq ft is the dominant unit for PEB supply contracts and must be shown to allow any budget comparison across listings.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per project vs per piece creates genuine price comparison confusion in this category; unit must be shown alongside any indicative price so buyers can interpret and compare figures correctly.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Span width is the primary structural determinant — it defines which aircraft can be accommodated, drives the entire frame design, and produces the largest price delta across values (Up To 30 m vs Above 60 m represents a multi-fold cost difference in steel tonnage and foundation load).

Hangar type (Defence, MRO, Cargo, Helicopter, General Aviation) is non-interchangeable — each imposes distinct fire suppression class, structural loading, door configuration, and regulatory compliance requirements that fundamentally change the design scope and price.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Tail height of the aircraft determines the minimum clear eave height required — this is a non-negotiable structural dimension that directly drives frame cost and is a primary buyer specification alongside span width.

The hangar door opening must exceed the aircraft's wingspan; buyers specify this dimension explicitly and it drives door system selection and structural header design — a separate and critical configurator from Door Type.

IS 875 wind zone and IS 1893 seismic zone determine structural steel tonnage and connection design; buyers in coastal or high-seismic regions specify this explicitly and it materially affects fabrication cost.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Clear span directly determines which aircraft the hangar can accommodate and is the single most important dimension sellers need to assess structural feasibility, steel tonnage, and project cost.

Door type (Sliding, Bi-Fold, Hydraulic, Fabric) determines operational workflow compatibility and is a major cost driver; sellers need this to scope the door system supply and confirm their fabrication capability.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the hangar is for general aviation storage, MRO operations, helicopter use, or defence — each imposes distinct fire suppression, structural loading, and regulatory compliance requirements that change the entire design scope.
